threats.abuse_case: A task reuses a revoked or expired capability to reach a service after its authority changed.
threats.mitigation: Capability tables carry revocation generations, leases, scope checks, and explicit rights projections. Shared fixed and paged handle arenas permanently retire slots at generation exhaustion within an arena lifetime, preserve exhaustion across reset and index rebuild, and refuse replacement without invalidating the last live handle. Endpoint reset preserves its generation history; task restore checks destination generations before retirement or grant changes. Capability batch admission, vault lending, delegation reuse and closed overlay-session reuse reject or skip exhausted slots before publishing new authority.

threats.abuse_case: A component bypasses typed component ports or native kernel mediation to obtain ambient process authority.
threats.mitigation: The native syscall surface, service contracts, and userspace launch provenance reject unsigned or synthetic launch paths.

threats.abuse_case: A boot artifact, policy, driver set, or userspace image is modified after signing.
threats.mitigation: Measured boot records bind every artifact digest and QEMU negative profiles fail closed on tamper.

threats.abuse_case: A rollback, interrupted write, or crash recovery path loses persistent state or exposes unredacted diagnostics.
threats.mitigation: Recovery, storage durability, root-slot corruption, and crash record gates require deterministic recovery and redacted summaries.

threats.abuse_case: A service or app hides a sensitive action behind a stale policy decision or missing denial explanation.
threats.mitigation: Policy mediation, denial explanations, event ledger records, and permission review services record explicit decisions.

threats.abuse_case: Malformed storage logs, oversized payloads, or torn records corrupt object or workspace state.
threats.mitigation: Storage volume replay validates root slots, checksums, payload bounds, segment counts, and quota behavior.

threats.abuse_case: A remote node replays, duplicates, or redirects sync frames without a trusted platform root.
threats.mitigation: Device graph authorization, durable replay rejection and policy remain test backed. Noise XX channels certify fresh X25519 keys with graph-authenticated Ed25519 device identities rooted in an independent pin. Both QEMU guests decrypt remote traffic and reject tampering and replay. Directional keys, complete datagram-header authentication, a bounded replay bitmap, erasure and live trust rechecks protect the channel. The bounded object receiver independently checks locally bound capabilities, writable network shares and selective policy before staging, rejects stale version writes, erases revoked or expired transfers, and issues receipts only after durable checkpoints. The two-guest gate reloads a received object from the target disk before acknowledging it. Peer authentication requires a non-exportable sealed signing lease and retires traffic keys on lease expiry, revocation, policy denial or key changes. Vault catalog v4 atomically checkpoints graph enrollment, rotation and revocation with sealed keys and credentials; restore requires an independent root pin and verifies inner graph signatures before publishing state. Failed durable mutations block subsequent enrollment operations. The TPM guest gate generates all peer keys, commits enrollment and authenticates with the restored graph and sealed keys after reboot; only the separate public-pin enrollment anchor remains fixture signed. Rollback-resistant generation floors remain external. Runtime admission now bounds established peers to four sessions, two operations per dispatch, eight accepted frames per peer per tick and a 30-second lifetime. It rejects unknown peers before cryptography, preserves unrelated receive traffic, retries driver-backpressured ciphertext on deadlines without advancing nonces, and rechecks authority before every send. Inactive tasks, lost devices, expiry and revocation close channels and erase staging; the two-node gate verifies sync-task suspension cleanup. Receive slots are reclaimed independently of unread unrelated packets; an active protocol reservation partitions the unchanged 32-slot backing into eight peer and 24 generic slots, so either stalled consumer leaves the other capacity. A separate four-slot handshake table shares the existing dispatch budget with object traffic and accepts only locally selected device pairs with live sync-service and sealed-key authority. Ten-second lifetimes and per-tick receive limits bound pending work; retries reuse exact ciphertext and queued duplicates do not amplify responses. Failed authentication closes the attempt instead of allocating a replacement from network input. Host loss tests cover all Noise flights and both encrypted confirmations, while both QEMU guests verify pending-handshake cleanup on task suspension. Final confirmation bytes survive successful handoff so application retries can recover a lost last delivery. The runtime sender independently binds a local read capability, network share and selective policy, pins source version and blob identity, and rechecks them before reads and cached egress. It streams bounded storage ranges without a second plaintext snapshot, pins the first authenticated destination offer, and rejects unsent-range or premature durable receipts. Lost application replies trigger fresh-nonce retries of idempotent requests; driver backpressure retains exact ciphertext. Host tests drop each object protocol leg and cover source edits, scope denial, revocation, failed durable barriers and invalid receipts; both QEMU guests use runtime sessions and prove sender and receiver retirement. Service-owned connections now replace borrowed transfer state with four generation-checked handles. Only authorized local opens allocate bounded coordination and receive bytes. Handoff rechecks authority and source version within the existing dispatch budget; release, expiry, authentication failure or task retirement removes protocol pointers before scrubbing and freeing allocations. Handle generations survive reset and never wrap. Tests cover stale handles, capacity, loss across handoff, changed authority and promotion failure without damaging another session. The two-node proof retires pending owners on storage suspension and active owners on sync suspension. Public enrollment now binds remote proof of possession and owner consent to an independently supplied root pin, without passing the remote private key to the authority. Signed publications authenticate all graph metadata and import verifies local sealed-key custody before a durable checkpoint. Known membership, generations, revocations and platform bindings cannot regress; duplicate messages do not grow history. Host tests cover separate disks and vaults, byte corruption, truncation, wrong pins and keys, same-generation rewrites, capacity and both durability barriers. The TPM cold/reboot proof now restores separately held device keys and public graphs from two vault catalogs; both vaults share one guest TPM. User approval, enrollment transport and independent rollback floors remain external. Rotation requests now prove successor possession and current-key consent over the prior generation and pinned owner root. The requesting device checkpoints both keys before emitting a proposal; the authority needs only the public proof and its own root lease. Approval rejects stale or competing generations and platform downgrades, while matching installed successors are idempotent. Crash tests cover preparation, approval and import at both durability barriers. TPM cold/reboot evidence restores the separate remote vault, authenticates with the successor and refuses its retired device key. Root rotation certificates now bind the exact predecessor consent and successor proof, preventing a different valid consent from authorizing retirement. Durable retirement requires the approved successor, preserves keys referenced by catalog signing, credentials, owner roots or trusted devices, and checks policy and audit before invalidating every lease and erasing the current record. Catalog v4 persists reusable slot generations, rejects resurrected IDs and changed live bindings, and restores no leases. Vault imports, generation, rotation, lending and revocation now preserve prior authority when the supplied audit backend fails. Unpublished key material is erased and its previous slot identity restored; paired lease arenas are preflighted before recording an approved lease. Failed replacement validation or provider calls cannot revoke old leases. Export bytes and signatures remain withheld on audit errors. Host regressions cover repeated failures beyond capacity, slot reuse and both revocation scopes. Audit acceptance is a serialized in-process boundary; durable retention remains an integration responsibility. Host tests cover repeated rotation beyond slot capacity, generation exhaustion and both durability barriers; TPM cold/reboot checks two rotations, slot reuse and refusal of retired IDs. Historical encrypted checkpoint versions remain retained, so this is logical retirement, not secure erasure. Independent rollback floors and lost-key recovery remain open. Production identity provisioning, discovery and connection provisioning, continuous convergence and typed secret/collection/event-stream protocols remain release blockers.

threats.abuse_case: Crash dumps or support bundles include secrets, capability tokens, raw memory, or private object names by default.
threats.mitigation: Crash summaries redact sensitive reason strings and the release policy denies raw memory capture by default.

threats.abuse_case: A restarted userspace driver keeps stale broker authority, DMA metadata, or port access.
threats.mitigation: Driver restart proofs reject stale authority, stale DMA/port access, and rebind fresh broker sessions by generation.
